A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the future of global public health will be defined by ubiquitous chronic disease prevention and management, emphasising risk factor identification and management; universal health coverage of high quality health services; and improved vital registration, which is prioritised by those preparing for societies with an ageing population.
the future of global public health is highly uncertain.

the future of global public health will require: 1. continued focus on solving the problems of the worst off, 2. strengthening and balancing universal health coverage with targeted interventions, 3. greater investment in the social and environmental determinants of health and the promotion of primary prevention of communicable and non-communicable diseases, 4. greater investment and attention to the health of women, children, and adolescents, 5. increased focus on improving human capital, as well as considerable health surveillance
The main takeaway from our work is that

while considerable progress has been made in improving the health of the population and much has been learned, the development world still has a long way to go in achieving the Sustainable Development Goals.

while there are clear developing country deficits across the health spectrum, developed countries also face notable public health challenges and health system limitations, particularly related to chronic diseases and mental health.
while there are clear developing country deficits across the health spectrum, the difference between countries can be large when we consider highly specific health challenges.
